_about: The graph portrait: every number it uses. The framework ships this file; a vault overrides any subset in state/portrait_targets.json (same shape, validated on load; an invalid override is rejected whole). `lifehug doctor` prints every effective value and where it came from. Rationale for each weight: system/research/life-portrait-targets.md. Keys starting with _ are comments.

targets._about: Relative target weight per entity type and kind (graph-vis D4: an owner table by type AND relation, not learned from citations). Within a type these rank kinds; across types, type_scale (below) says how big a type is next to a parent. A roster entry or a roadmap focus with `portrait_weight` replaces the table weight for that entity.

tiers._about: Multiplier on the table weight when the entity's page is a Focus page, by Focus tier. none = not a Focus.

type_scale._about: v380 (owner observation 2026-09-30: 'the biggest things would be my dad and my mom, to tell a story about myself'). On the SHARED scale (calibration.mode = shared) every entity's target = table weight x tier x type_scale[type] x the anchor scale, so these are fractions of a parent's target. The owner's provisional numbers, revisitable; one-line rationale each in system/research/life-portrait-targets.md (Amendment 2026-09-30). A type missing here scales 1.0. Ignored in per_type mode.

kinds._about: How an entity's kind is read. age_frame_pattern: a period page slug matching this regex is an age frame.

calibration._about: Puts table weights on the credit scale. mode shared (v380, default): ONE scale for the whole portrait, anchored on people - the anchor scale is the anchor `quantile` of credit / (weight x tier x type_scale) over the credited anchor members (type anchor.type, kind in anchor.kinds; 1.0 = the best-told parent/spouse/partner sits exactly on its target), and every type's scale is type_scale[type] x that anchor scale. With no credited anchor member the anchor falls back to the same quantile over every credited entity. mode per_type (v378): each type calibrates on itself - scale = the `quantile` of credit / (weight x tier) over the type's credited members; a type with fewer than min_peers credited members borrows the median scale of the other types. exclude_kinds are never calibrated on in either mode (the owner's own person page duplicates the hub).

credit._about: How a source's telling is shared. split: equal = a source held by n entity pages gives 1/n to each (owner ruling 2026-09-29); whole = 1 to each. Answers under answer_prefixes: rule listed = every page that lists the answer holds it; tagged = only pages the answer's classification tags. Other sources under classified_prefixes (conversation, email, manual, landmarks) earn credit only for the entities their CURRENT classification tags as subjects in tag_fields (the relevance gate: never a bare name occurrence; an unclassified source earns nothing). A person tag needs at least min_person_mentions.

drawing._about: Pixels. Fill and ring share one scale: radius = radius_min + radius_span * sqrt(value / largest target on the canvas), so area is proportional to credit and the ring sits at the target. The fill is capped at the ring; a node told past its target (over = told/target - 1 > 0) gets a second, thinner ring over_ring_offset pixels outside it. A node with no credit draws at radius_min. Relationship edges: width = edge_min + edge_span * min(1, told/target).

focus_halo._about: A_FOCUS_WEARS_GOLD (owner 2026-09-30: 'a golden orb around the intended size'). A static gold halo (no animation, graph-vis D11/D12) drawn `gap` pixels outside the target ring (outside the over-told ring when there is one) on every entity that is a roadmap Focus whose phase is in `phases`, resolved through the same focus_pages join the ring uses. Colour #rrggbb; width in pixels.

project_halo._about: The project mark: a solid (never dashed, D18) halo of a second colour, `gap` pixels outside everything else drawn around a project node (outside the gold halo when the project is also a Focus).

doctor._about: How many rows doctor lists per type: the largest gaps, and the most over-told (told past target - the honest sign that a tag is applied to almost everything).
